title: Query frontier for two-round single-permutation Even--Mansour
summary: Determine the tight outer-versus-inner query-security boundary for two-round single-permutation Even--Mansour with a good one-master-key schedule.

formal_statement.body: Let $N=2^n$ and let $\operatorname{EMSP}[n,2,\gamma]$ be the source construction: one public random $n$-bit permutation is reused in both rounds, and the three round keys are derived from one $n$-bit master key by a good schedule $\gamma$ in the sense of Definition 2. For a computationally unbounded adversary making $q_e$ adaptive two-sided cipher queries and $q_p$ adaptive two-sided permutation queries, determine the asymptotically tight boundary between negligible and non-negligible strong-PRP advantage throughout the still-open region of Figure 2, up to the source's polylogarithmic convention.

scope.domain: Information-theoretic strong-PRP security of two-round single-permutation Even--Mansour
assumptions: One public random n-bit permutation is reused in both rounds
All three round keys are derived from one n-bit master key by a Definition 2 good schedule
The adversary is computationally unbounded and may query the cipher and public permutation adaptively in both directions
scope.unresolved_remainder: The 2019 attacks improve the attainable low-data and low-memory tradeoffs but explicitly leave a gap. Every remaining $(q_e,q_p)$ regime between the proved security bound and known attacks for the exact single-permutation, one-master-key construction still needs matching bounds.

citations.label: Chen--Lampe--Lee--Seurin--Steinberger, two-round EMSP query-frontier question
citations.locator: Revised full version dated 2014-12-18, Figure 2 on p. 6 and Section 6.1 on p. 34

progress.summary: The revised full version marks the single-permutation Figure 2 query regimes beyond its proved bound as open.
A 3-XOR reduction yields new low-data and low-memory attacks and a faster asymptotic attack, while the paper explicitly retains a gap to the security proof.
